page.layout: One printed page. Running head at top centre; page number top left. Single column of verse and prose with italic headings. Faint show-through from the facing page appears in the right margin and is left out. No marginal notes; the small marks at line ends are not text.

main_text.l: Abfit ego vos discipulos dicámve, putémve,
Discendi per quos est via strata mihi.
Dat mihi suggestum, nomen fortasse magistri,
Nam dum quærendi vos ardor pungit amórque,
Multa meis nunquam debere negabo magistris:
Discere qui facilis, qui scita tenere fidelis,
Non leuis his istæc, iftis hæc vertere cœptis,
Adspirante Deo studiis, breue nomen habebit-

l.i: Rex quod licet, Tyrannus quod libet, facit.

main_text.l: Si sit in alterius littera versa vicem.
Scribito C, Regem facies: B pinge, tyrannum:
Quod libet hic etenim, quod licet, ille facit.

l.i: Ad votum Socratis, quo optabat se intus & foris

main_text.l: Intus quo petiit pulcher & esse foris.

page.notes: Show-through from the facing page at the right margin is omitted. Some ink-blotted marks near line ends are doubtful. The word "Sed" at the foot is set at the right and may be a catchword or the start of the next line; it is copied as printed.
